headline: Bull's 'oversold' RSI is 36-38 in a trend where the 1h close (74,207) is below its own lower Bollinger band (74,234), their VWAP target is my short entry zone, and their first target pays only 0.84R with a December Fed hike priced into CPI.
argument:
Bull's case rests on four claims. None survives a check against the data.

RSI: 36.6 (5m), 36.4 (15m) and 38.6 (1h) is not oversold. Oversold is below 30. The 1h window is down 8.51%, price is below the 1h SMA200 (76,697.33), and the 1h MACD histogram is -63.41, deeper than the previous -49.22. In a downtrend RSI sits in the 30s for hours. The 1h close is also below its lower Bollinger band (74,234.15), which is a trending move, not a mean-reversion setup.

Fear: Fear & Greed is 32, up from 29, while price falls. That is not capitulation, and funding is still positive (+0.0088%), so longs are paying to stay in and have not been flushed. CoinDesk today (Nov 10): traders are pricing a December Fed hike and Waller reportedly backs one even if inflation cools. That is a one-sided CPI risk for an asset sitting at the bottom of its range.

VWAP target: the UTC-day VWAP is 74,738.88. It coincides with the 1h EMA21 (74,734.20) and sits just above the 1h EMA9 (74,562.86). That is where sellers wait, and it is exactly my short entry zone.

Stop and R:R: Bull enters at 74,150 with a stop at 73,450 (risk 700). The first target, VWAP, pays about 591, which is 0.84R. Their 1:1.8 only exists if price clears three resistance layers to 75,400, with 1h volume at 0.15x its 20-bar average. The order book swung from 0.17 to 0.44 bids/asks between pulls, so I weight it lightly, but it is still ask-heavy at 741,176 vs 1,703,416 USDT. Selling rallies into 74,450-74,650 gives better reward-to-risk than buying into them.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: RSI 36.0 / 36.1 / 38.5 is a washed-out zone where sellers run out of fuel
rebuttals.response: RSI under 30 is oversold; 36-39 is not. The 1h RSI is 38.6 with the MACD histogram deepening (-63.41 vs -49.22) and price below the 1h SMA200 (76,697.33). RSI reads low in every sustained decline. The 1h close is below its lower Bollinger band (74,234.15), a trend signal.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: Fear & Greed 32, up from 29, plus funding of only +0.0088% means a contrarian long
rebuttals.response: A reading of 32 is mild fear, not capitulation. It rose 3 points while price fell, so sentiment is not washed out. Funding is positive, not negative, so longs are still paying and no short squeeze is loaded. Add a Fed hike now priced for December (CoinDesk, Nov 10) and the CPI skew is hawkish, not neutral.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: target 74,741 session VWAP (partial) and 75,400 (1h upper BB)
rebuttals.response: VWAP (74,738.88) is stacked on the 1h EMA21 (74,734.20) and just above the 1h EMA9 (74,562.86), the area I sell. Reaching it earns about 591 against 700 of risk (0.84R). 75,400 is also above the 1h SMA50 (75,006.71) and the 5m recent high (74,996.01), with 1h volume at 0.15x average. The 75,400 target needs a regime change.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: stop 73,450 below the 1h 50-bar low 73,510, R:R 1:1.8
rebuttals.response: The stop is 700 away (1.66 times the 1h ATR of 422) while the realistic first target is about 591 away. Their 1:1.8 holds only if the 75,400 target is hit. They also plan to add size only if the 74,058 24h low holds, and a hawkish CPI gap through it hits a stop that may slip below 73,450.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: the selloff is on thin volume, so it is not capitulation and a bounce is likely
rebuttals.response: Thin volume means thin demand too. A bounce on 0.15x 1h volume has no buyers behind it and fades at VWAP. Low volume before a CPI print also makes the move that follows larger, and the CPI skew is hawkish.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: ETF outflows (-1.28B) are already priced in because price holds near 74k
rebuttals.response: Price is 8.51% lower over the 1h window and under every moving average. 'Holding 74k' is a drift at the 24h low (74,058.7) that has not bounced. Nothing in the data shows buyers absorbing the outflow.

plan.entry: short on a bounce into 74,450-74,650 (1h EMA9 74,562.86 area, below VWAP 74,738.88); no chase below 74,150
plan.risk_reward: 1:2.1 to 73,510 and 1:3.1 to 73,000 from entry 74,550 (risk 500). This corrects the R1 figures of 1:1.6 and 1:2.4, which understated the ratios
plan.timeframe: intraday, 4-8 hours; flat or half size through the US CPI print
